newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: At least 10 die in Colombia cement plant disaster.
newsitem.headline: At least 10 die in Colombia cement plant disaster.

text.p: The death toll from a fiery disaster at a cement plant in central Colombia rose to at least 10 on Saturday after five more workers died from severe burn injuries overnight, hospital officials said.

Friday's accident at the Caracolito plant in the city of Ibague was caused by a blockage in one of the pre-heaters that a mix of raw materials pass through before being blended at extremely high temperatures into cement, witnesses and Fire Department officials said.

Carlos Navarrete, an electrician at the plant, told Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper that a sudden "roar" was heard as a cloud of red-hot material exploded through a conduit and rained down on his co-workers like napalm.
"It all happened so fast that the guys didn't have time to react," he said.

Marlen Vela, a spokeswoman for the Social Security hospital in Ibague where all 17 victims of the accident were taken, told Reuters that 10 had died as of early Saturday from third-degree burns covering as much as 80 percent of their "mummified" bodies.
Five others were in critical condition, she added, saying four had been airlifted to hospitals in the capital Bogota.
The three-year-old Caracolito plant, which industry experts describe as state-of-the-art, is owned and operated by Cementos Diamante, a subsidiary of Mexican cement giant Cemento Mexicanos (Cemex).

Juan Romero, Cemex's chief of operations in Colombia, issued a statement late on Friday lamenting the "unfortunate accident" and saying it would be fully investigated to prevent anything like it from occurring again.
